evidence: Catalog.reserve checks canReserve and throws 'Insufficient stock' when stock is short. This is a domain rule.
Catalog.getAvailableStock returns total minus reserved. This is a domain calculation.
Catalog.release uses Math.max(0, ...) so reserved stock never goes below zero. This is a domain rule.
The Map fields hold the aggregate's in-memory state. There is no I/O, database, repository or framework code in the file.

parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/domain/Catalog.ts is a domain aggregate. It keeps products, stock and reserved quantities in its own state and enforces the business rules for that state. It works out available stock as total minus reserved. canReserve and reserve stop the catalog from reserving more than is available. release keeps the reserved count from going below zero. The Maps hold the aggregate's own in-memory state. They are not a persistence mechanism: there is no database, ORM, file or repository access. The file also has no transport, HTTP, framework, serialization or orchestration logic. Application use cases inject Catalog and coordinate it, which is the expected split between domain and application. Every responsibility fits the domain layer.
